AI Proficiency Levels

Four levels. S3729C sits at Level 3.

Tap a level to see its description.

The hallmark of Level 3

Students stop using AI tools and start building them.

Users of AIBuilders of AI tools

Build for real-world use

Customise or build AI tools for real-world use, with reference to industry trends and practices.

Students pick a real gap in their workplace or volunteer work, then build and deploy a working app with Kiro.

Account for usability and bias

Account for usability, bias etc.

Apps are tested with peers, family and friends. Real data flows into R Shiny, where students question what it can and cannot tell them.

Embed ethics early

Embed ethics early in the developmental process.

Privacy and honest claims are written into the requirements: nicknames not names, video processed on-device, results framed as screening, not diagnosis.

Why not Level 4? L4 is system-level design with architecture and governance, usually in capstone projects. L3 is where most modules can realistically land.

Metacognitive prompting

Same tool. Different thinking.

Normal prompting

"AI, improve my dashboard."

Fast results, but students may not know why changes were made or whether they suit their users.

VS

Metacognitive prompting

"Evaluate my dashboard, explain what should improve and why, then implement the changes."

Results grounded in evidence, purpose and users. The student stays the decision-maker.

Tap each step to see the question it adds to a prompt.
